questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking country, renowned university, nice weather and explore Austrialian culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy if you read through the emails that were sent to you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Lived three different places throughout the stay. Found the first one through the Facebook group named 'Young Danes in Sydney'. Next one was also through a Facebook group for accommodation. Found the last one through mouth-to-mouth which I would highly recommend. Consult with people that have been to Sydney and here if they have any recs.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Accommodation in  Australia is expensive and especially in Sydney. You can easily pay $400-500 AUD per week per person - or even more. Living in a shared house is however often cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You got sent a course catalogue from the host university which you could browse through and was pretty convenient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not consult with anyone before choosing courses (units).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful in registering for all classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Economics students can register for most economics, business and finance courses in a broader sense. Both UCPH and USYD will approve them if they should be transferred to electives . I heard from people studying Law that they had more problems registering for the courses they wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my courses ranged from same to lower level compared to UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In 3/4 of my courses (units), there were both lectures and tutorials similar to UCPH.
There were mandatory hand-ins and mid-semester exams that counted towards the final grade in most of the courses.
In one of my courses, attendance was mandatory. Although, USYD states that 80-90% attendance in classes is mandatory, this is not the case for all courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FINC3015: Financial Valuation: A case study approach
ECON6024: Private Equity
IBUS5003: Global Business
QBUS5001: Quantitative Analytics for Business

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For students who are into finance, I would recommend FINC3015. In this course, we did valuations on two publicly listed companies which we had to hand in that counted towards the final grade. You really learn how to apply the theoretical that you learn on by constructing your own set of valuations and assumptions in Excel. However, I cannot recommend attending the lectures as the lecturer was not really good and used the slides of the former lecturer. Video material and tutorials were available online. Also, I spoke with an Aussie who previously attended the course who told me that employers in Australia regarded it as the go-to finance course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Student visa in Australia (subclass 500) is incredibly expensive. I payed $2,000 AUD and I believe this is now raised to $2,500 AUD. In hindsight, I would have looked into whether I could have used a working visa instead. Also, you need an OSHC which is a health insurance to apply for the student visa that costs around $250 AUD.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Barista coffee is cheap compared to DK but alcohol is 2-3x the price in Denmark in liquor stores.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I signed up the university gym which included aquatics as well. Also, there are all sorts of societies that you can join for free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't really use any apart from the gym membership.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on Surf Camp, do a roadtrip along the east coast with friends, go to Melbourne to watch Australian Open or the F1 GP if you are there at the right time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Australia is a wonderful mixture of the UK and US, and Aussies are extremely friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really. Almost no Australians take a post grad (master) so most of the other students are on exchange or studying abroad.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid-back but also very active/sporty culture and lifestyle in Sydney.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Talk to people who's been in Sydney to get recs on accommodation.
2. Put on positive hat and say yes to any adventure and opportunity that occurs
3. Although, there is a lot of assessment throughout the year, you will be fine and pass.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring a physical calculator as all exams are with pen and paper - and no aids except a calculator.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Enjoy living in another country on the other side of the planet.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Also being so far away from home so it's more challenging for people to visit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
